newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks plunge 4.32 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks plunge 4.32 pct in late trade.

text.p: Jakarta stocks plunged in late trading on Friday on rupiah worries as the currency further weakened against the dollar, brokers said.
The composite index fell 27.79 points, or 4.32 percent, to 615.22 points, a new year-low, at 0840 GMT. Decliners led gainers by 154 to nine with 20 issues unchanged.
Fifty-one stocks, out of the around 250 listed, also touched year-lows. Total turn-over was estimated at 394 billion rupiah.
"The market turned panicky after the rupiah fell to 2,900 (against the dollar). Players, both local and foreign, were in a selling spree after the fall," one broker said.

Tom Inglis, head of research with ING Barings, said uncertainties in the market were likely to remain due to the rupiah and that market psychology was likely to rule over fundamentals. "It's a blue day today. We expect the weak market to remain for around three months," he said.
The panic selling both by local and foreign players was across the board, pushing around one-fifth of the listed firms to touch year-lows, brokers said.
Blue chips banks BII, BNI, pulp and paper firm Indah Kiat and telecommunications giant Telkom were among the hardest hit.
